simple.meaning: דָּוֶה (dâveh) is a Hebrew word meaning “sick (especially in menstruation).” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: דָּוֶה (H1739) appears 5 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Leviticus 15:33, with occurrences in Leviticus, Isaiah, Lamentations.

simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in דָּוֶה (H1739) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: דָּוֶה (dâveh) / H1739 is traced through Leviticus 15:33, Leviticus 20:18, Isaiah 30:22, Lamentations 1:13 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

definitions.usage: faint, menstruous cloth, she that is sick, having sickness.
definitions.full: H1739. daveh דָּוֶה adjective faint, unwell — דָּוֶה Lam 5:17 , feminine דָּוָה Lev 15:33 3 t.; 1 faint , Lam 1:13 (|| שֹׁמֵמָה ) 5:17 . 2 unwell, menstruous Lev 15:33 ; 20:18 ; Isa 30:22 דָּוָה perhaps = דָוָה כְּלִי De.

occurrences.englishText: and of her who has her period, and of a man or woman who has a discharge, and of him who lies with her who is unclean.

“ ‘If a man lies with a woman having her monthly period, and uncovers her nakedness, he has made her fountain naked, and she has uncovered the fountain of her blood. Both of them shall be cut off from among their people.
You shall defile the overlaying of your engraved images of silver, and the plating of your molten images of gold. You shall cast them away as an unclean thing. You shall tell it, “Go away!”
“From on high has he sent fire into my bones,
For this our heart is faint.
